group: PSI Score: Pneumonia Severity Index for CAP
question:
Patient note:
A 63-year-old woman who lives alone in a single-story house and still drives herself to weekly church choir practice presented to the emergency department early this morning after three days of gradually worsening cough and exertional breathlessness that culminated in an episode of lightheadedness while walking from her bedroom to the kitchen; she denied syncope, and she had taken no over-the-counter medications, used no home nebulizers, and received no supplemental oxygen before arrival because she “wanted the doctors to see the real picture.” Her medical history includes an anterior wall myocardial infarction five years ago that left her with systolic dysfunction (most recent echocardiogram six months earlier showed an ejection fraction in the mid-30s with mild left atrial enlargement) and a small right parietal cerebrovascular event two years ago from which she recovered full strength but remains on low-dose aspirin. She follows a cardiologist, takes carvedilol 12.5 mg twice daily and sacubitril-valsartan 24/26 mg twice daily, has never required dialysis, has no history of chronic kidney disease or renal insufficiency, has normal liver enzymes on prior panels and has never been diagnosed with cirrhosis, chronic hepatitis, or any chronic liver disorder, and has no record of malignant disease. She quit smoking two decades ago after a ten-pack-year exposure, drinks a glass of red wine with Sunday dinner only, and denies any recreational drug use. Vaccination records retrieved from the state registry confirm completion of both pneumococcal series and an influenza vaccine given at her local pharmacy last autumn. On EMS arrival to her home she was sitting upright on the couch in moderate respiratory distress but answering questions lucidly; the crew transported her without intravenous access, fluids, or oxygen so as not to confound initial measurements. In triage she appeared alert, oriented, and anxious to cooperate, speaking in full sentences but pausing for breath after every few words. Skin was warm and dry, conjunctivae were pink, and capillary refill was brisk. Untreated vital signs on ambient air at sea-level were: oral temperature 99.8 °F, regular but thready pulse 145 beats per minute confirmed on telemetry, non-invasive blood pressure 119/72 mm Hg verified manually, respiratory rate 28 breaths per minute with mild suprasternal retraction, and fingertip pulse oximetry 96 % while seated upright. Jugular venous pulsation was estimated at 4 cm above the sternal angle at 45°, identical to notes from her cardiology visit. Cardiac auscultation revealed a rapid S1 and S2 with a soft third sound and no new murmurs or pericardial rub. Lungs transmitted coarse inspiratory crackles over the right mid-lung field posteriorly and faint scattered rhonchi on the left; percussion remained resonant throughout, and costophrenic angles were sharp. The abdomen was flat, soft, and nontender with no hepatosplenomegaly; there was no pedal edema. A focused neurologic screen showed equal pupils, intact extra-ocular movements, symmetric facial expression, 5/5 strength in all extremities, and fluent speech, without dysmetria or aphasia. Finger-stick glucose performed before venipuncture measured 141 mg/dL. Venous blood drawn within ten minutes of arrival—before any saline flushes—returned sodium 142 mEq/L, potassium 3.8 mEq/L, chloride 104 mEq/L, bicarbonate 22 mEq/L, blood urea nitrogen 18 mg/dL, and creatinine 0.9 mg/dL, values very close to those in her primary-care records. Complete blood count demonstrated leukocytes 13.6 × 10⁹/L with 86 % segmented neutrophils, hematocrit 44 %, hemoglobin 15.1 g/dL, and platelets 248 × 10⁹/L. A right radial arterial sample obtained while she continued to breathe room air revealed an alkalemic pH of 7.73, PaCO₂ 22 mm Hg, PaO₂ 107 mm Hg, and calculated bicarbonate 23 mEq/L, consistent with a primary respiratory alkalosis from tachypnea and no hypoxemia. Serum lactate was 1.3 mmol/L. Twelve-lead electrocardiography showed sinus tachycardia at 146 bpm with nonspecific ST-T wave flattening but no acute ischemic pattern compared with prior tracings. A portable postero-anterior chest radiograph acquired before any treatment displayed a patchy consolidation in the right middle lobe with air bronchograms, preserved diaphragmatic contours, and no blunting of the costophrenic angles or layering fluid. Two peripheral sets of blood cultures, an expectorated sputum sample for Gram stain and culture, urinary antigens for common bacterial pathogens, and a multiplex respiratory viral panel were dispatched to the laboratory prior to antibiotic initiation. Up to the time of this note she has received neither intravenous crystalloids, vasopressors, bronchodilators, diuretics, nor supplemental oxygen beyond the ambient 21 %, and she has not been given antipyretics or analgesics; therefore every physiologic observation, laboratory value, and imaging finding detailed above reflects her untreated presentation.

Question: What is the patient's Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI)? You should use the patient's medical values and health status when they were first admitted to the hospital prior to any treatment.
solution:
The Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI) sums demographic, comorbidity, examination, laboratory, and radiographic points at presentation.
- Demographics: For a woman, use age minus 10: 63 − 10 = 53 points. She lives at home, so nursing-home residence adds 0.
- Comorbidities: Systolic heart failure adds 10; prior stroke adds 10 for cerebrovascular disease. No malignancy, liver disease, or renal disease: 0 additional points.
- Examination: Pulse 145/min meets the ≥125/min threshold: 10 points. She is oriented, respiratory rate 28 is below 30/min, systolic BP 119 is at least 90 mm Hg, and temperature 99.8 °F (37.7 °C) is neither <35 nor ≥40 °C: 0 additional points.
- Labs and imaging: Arterial pH 7.73 does not meet the low-pH criterion (<7.35). BUN 18 is below 30 mg/dL, sodium 142 is at least 130 mEq/L, glucose 141 is below 250 mg/dL, hematocrit 44% is at least 30%, and room-air PaO₂ 107 is at least 60 mm Hg. No pleural effusion: 0 points.
Total = 53 + 10 + 10 + 10 = 83.
Final answer: 83
